faq.a1: Trisle is a small overlay app that recreates the iPhone's Dynamic Island on Android. It floats a pill-shaped capsule at the top of your screen — above every app — and morphs it to show live alerts, notifications and ongoing activities like music playback, timers, calls and Google Maps navigation.
faq.a2: Trisle runs on Android 7.0 and above, and is fully optimized for Android 12 through 16. It adapts to any camera cutout — centered, left or right — so it looks native on virtually any device.
faq.a3: No. The island renders in true black, which modern OLED panels effectively switch off, and it runs as a low-priority foreground service that only wakes on real system events. When idle, it can hide itself completely to free the GPU and compositor.
faq.a4: Completely. Everything — notification parsing, media session sync, navigation text extraction — happens strictly on your device. Trisle collects nothing, transmits nothing and contains no analytics or tracking SDKs. On the lock screen, notification content can be redacted automatically.
faq.a5: Android only allows apps to read notification content through the Notification Listener API, which powers the music island, navigation capsule, timers and smart alert banners. The permission is granted through a system settings screen you can revoke at any time.
faq.a6: Trisle is a one-time purchase — €3.99, once, including VAT. Checkout is handled by Polar.sh, which acts as the merchant of record and processes payments, taxes and invoices securely. You receive an instant download and lifetime updates. No subscription, no recurring charges.
faq.a7: No. Trisle is an independent product built for Android. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Apple Inc. 'Dynamic Island' is a trademark of Apple Inc., referenced here only to describe the interaction style Trisle recreates.
faq.a8: Easy — if Trisle isn't for you, you get a full refund anytime within 7 days of your purchase. No questions asked. Just contact support with your order details and Polar.sh processes it back to your original payment method.
faq.a9: No. Trisle installs like any regular app and asks for two standard Android permissions — display over other apps, and notification access. Both are granted through Android's own system dialogs, one tap each. No root, no modified system files, no special tools.
faq.label: FAQ
faq.q2: Which Android versions does it support?
faq.q5: Why does it need notification access?
faq.q9: Do I need to root my phone?
